points.text: Heavy compute and simulation time requirements limit real-world scalability
Only 62.5% of tasks ran fully automatically; true autonomy not achieved
No comparison with other meta-agent systems that could design FL setups
No standard deviations reported despite LLM and simulation stochasticity
No comparison with code-synthesis pipelines such as SWE-Agent, AutoGPT, Voyager, CodeAct
No quantitative comparison to simple tools like Copilot or Cursor given human verification
No confidence intervals, standard deviations or number of runs for reported results
Architecture is generic multi-agent code synthesis; FL framing comes only from templates
No new mechanism beyond prior agent frameworks, which are not referenced; novelty unjustified
AgentFL-Bench uses the same structured schema Helmsman expects, creating evaluation circularity
No test with paraphrased, incomplete or out-of-schema prompts
FedAvg/FedProx baselines measure learning accuracy, not synthesis performance; not comparable
No ablations on prompt wording, number of agents, LLM choice or agent roles
Runtime, LLM API usage and memory costs not quantified relative to alternatives
No variances, error bars, run counts or significance tests in main tables
Whether baselines used identical splits, models, hyperparameters is deferred to appendix
Data splits, client counts and configuration not summarized in main paper
Human-in-the-loop makes experiments manipulable and unfair versus fully automated methods
Paper is a system report; needs ablations to justify each design component
No baselines against single strong LLM, Claude Code, OpenHands or AIDE-style systems
Multi-agent design, L2 diagnosis, RAG, self-reflection, HITL are not ablated
Claim that single-agent approaches exceed capacity is unsupported
Unclear which results were autonomous vs human-assisted; human input not quantified
Baselines appear untuned off-the-shelf methods, loosely matched to tasks
Q7 and Q8 specialized values identical (63.62), likely copy error
Iterative selection criterion unclear; human approval may use test accuracy, risking leakage
Helmsman loses to specialized methods in about half the tasks; 'often superior' overstated
Small differences without variance; tables report no seeds, CIs or run counts
Q16 gain implausible; replay violates exemplar-free setting, no replay baseline
Generated code not shown; privacy constraints and leakage cannot be verified
Replay plus distillation is well known, so algorithmic novelty not demonstrated
No per-task success rate, attempts or specification-faithfulness measures
No token, dollar or wall-clock cost reported
No robustness evaluation across LLM backbones or seeds
'Rigorous and reproducible' claim lacks stated protocol release
Benchmark designed by same group, no held-out tasks; some baselines are authors' own
Tasks are small image datasets with Flower strategies; system-level claim weak
No tests of robustness to changing conditions and no user study of effort
Deployment-ready claims and production framework contrast untested; simulator only
L2 heuristics on 5-round logs cannot certify semantic correctness
No analysis of failure modes, iteration statistics or plan-ignoring code
Promotional tone; intro and related work spend space on generic agent narrative
Section 6 title typo 'Disucssion'
Hyperparameters, baseline tuning, selection and run counts in appendix or absent
Generic baselines limited to FedAvg/FedProx; stronger methods omitted

P.summary: High computational/simulation cost unquantified, limiting scalability
Only 62.5% of tasks fully automatic; autonomy not achieved
Human-in-the-loop makes comparisons manipulable or unfair
No comparison with other agent or code-generation systems
No variance, confidence intervals or number of runs reported
Architecture is generic, not intrinsically tied to federated learning
Limited novelty versus prior agent frameworks, not referenced
Benchmark circular: tasks share schema Helmsman is designed for
No robustness test to paraphrased or unstructured prompts
FL baselines measure accuracy, not system-synthesis performance
Baseline fairness details scattered in appendix
Key configuration details missing from main text

Q.summary: No agent or code-generation system baselines
Baselines untuned, off-the-shelf and loosely matched
Identical values for Q7 and Q8 suggest copy error
No seeds, variance or run counts in performance tables
Q16 result implausible; replay conflicts with exemplar-free setting
Q16 'novel combination' is a known recipe
No robustness across LLM backbones or seeds
Benchmark built by same authors, no held-out tasks
Motivation claims untested (dynamic robustness, effort reduction)
Key experimental details in appendix or absent
Generic baselines only FedAvg and FedProx
